models_evaluated: GPT (four prompt-engineered variants, including Optimized Features Model)

links.outcome: LLM NPV and accuracy versus ED clinicians on PECARN head injury risk classification
links.effect: Optimized Features Model NPV 0.98, accuracy 0.89 versus ED clinicians NPV 0.99, accuracy 0.92; all models had high NPV comparable to PEM physicians.
links.quote: The GPT model with the highest combination of NPV and accuracy was the prompt-engineered "Optimized Features Model" (NPV = 0.98, accuracy = 0.89), which performed similarly to that of the ED clinicians in both NPV (0.99) and accuracy (0.92).

unlisted_practices: prompt engineering of an LLM to extract clinical decision rule features from ED notes

screen.reason: The study evaluates the diagnostic accuracy and safety (NPV) of LLMs in extracting features and applying the PECARN pediatric head injury algorithm from retrospective ED notes. It evaluates prompt engineering/model variants rather than a health system deployment practice or safeguard.
